newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian mining chief welcomes tax reform debate.
newsitem.headline: Australian mining chief welcomes tax reform debate.

text.p: Minerals Council of Australia president Nick Stump on Thursday welcomed the government's recognition of the need to revamp the country's taxation system.

Stump said the tax system should treat tax payers more equitably. The government should also consider altering the system to ensure it caused little distortion to resource use, while minimising administrative and compliance burdens, he said.
"The prime minister's recognition of the need for tax reform down the track is a welcome sign that he recognises the need to address this issue," Stump told the council's annual seminar.
Earlier on Thursday, Southcorp Holdings Ltd chief executive Graham Kraehe told a business luncheon that Australia's future competitiveness depended on tax reform.

Prime Minister John Howard and Treasurer Peter Costello have both pushed the need for tax reform in recent weeks and have refused to rule out the introduction of a consumption tax if the Liberal-National government won a second term in power.
Polls published this week have shown increasing voter support for a goods and services tax (GST), which is paid when a consumer buys a good or service.
